title: Dogwood Vase
subject: objects
alt: A round, wide-shouldered yellow earthenware vase painted with large deep-pink dogwood flowers on thin brown branches, with a speckled turquoise rim, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint the yellow vase as one round shape first, then drop the flowers onto it once it is dry.
tip: Keep the flowers loose: four petals and a dot of green for each is enough.
curationNote: One clear object on a plain grey ground, painted with bold simple flowers. Good for warm yellows.

title: Woodland Plant Study
subject: botanical
alt: A watercolour study of a small woodland plant with fuzzy olive-green heart-shaped leaves, tiny pink flowers on a thin reddish stem and fine roots, beside a separate bare sprig, on plain cream paper.
prompt: This is already a watercolour. Match its washes: one pale green per leaf, darkened at the edge.
tip: Pull the roots and the stem with the very tip of a small brush, in one movement each.
curationNote: One focus subject on plain paper, already a watercolour. A lovely study to copy stroke for stroke.

title: Apple Blossom Vase
subject: objects
alt: A tall cylindrical cobalt blue earthenware vase painted with a branch of white and pink apple blossom and olive-green leaves, with a thin gold rim, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Leave the blossom as paper and paint the deep blue round it.
tip: Build the blue in two layers; one heavy layer dries patchy.
curationNote: One clear object on a plain grey ground. Deep blue with pale blossom is good practice for leaving the paper.

title: Bird-Shaped Vessel
subject: creatures
alt: A pale earthenware jug shaped like a bird, with a tall fan-shaped crest, a long beak and a spout rising from its back, standing on a round foot against a plain grey background.
prompt: Pale on grey. Paint the background round the bird and keep the bird itself to two soft greys.
tip: Soften the shadow side into the paper while it is damp, so the body looks round.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp. A pale shape with soft shadows.

title: Faience Jar
subject: objects
alt: A small squat Egyptian faience jar with a flared rim and base, in mottled turquoise and blue-green with darker speckles, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Wet the jar, drop in turquoise and green, and let them mottle on their own.
tip: Spatter a few darker specks once the wash is nearly dry.
curationNote: One small, simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp. A quick warm-up.

title: Red Clay Amphora
subject: objects
alt: A weathered red terracotta storage jar with a round body, a flared mouth and two small loop handles, its surface flecked with pale patches, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint the round body first in one warm wash, then add the pale patches by lifting.
tip: Lift the pale patches with a damp tissue while the red is still wet.
curationNote: One clear object on a plain grey ground, sharp. A simple round shape with a weathered surface.

title: Greek Bronze Horse
subject: creatures
alt: A small stylised Greek bronze horse with a long thin body, tall straight legs and a tube-like muzzle, standing on an openwork base, with a green patina, against a plain grey background.
prompt: This horse is nearly all straight lines. Paint each leg in one stroke.
tip: Drop a little viridian into the wet grey-green so the patina looks mottled rather than flat.
curationNote: One simple, stylised shape on a plain grey ground, sharp throughout.

title: Bronze Cat
subject: creatures
alt: A slender Egyptian bronze cat sitting upright with its tail curled round its front feet and its ears pricked, on a pale block against a plain grey background.
prompt: Get the silhouette right first: ears, long neck, round haunch. The rest is shading.
tip: Mix the bronze from burnt umber and a little burnt sienna, and leave a thin light edge down the back.
curationNote: One clear subject on a plain grey ground, sharp. A simple upright silhouette.

title: Turquoise Glass Vase
subject: objects
alt: A faceted opaque turquoise glass vase with a round, many-sided body, a tall straight neck and a flared foot, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint each facet as its own flat wash, a little lighter or darker than its neighbour.
tip: Leave a hairline gap between facets so they stay crisp.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp, in one bright colour.

title: Persimmon-Wood Box
subject: objects
alt: A long rectangular lidded box in persimmon wood, its orange grain streaked with black, with a small brass hasp on the front, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint the three faces as three different values of the same orange, then add the dark streaks.
tip: Pull the dark grain streaks along the length in one stroke each, into damp paint.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp. A clean box shape with bold wood grain.

title: Small Plant Study
subject: botanical
alt: A watercolour of one small upright plant with narrow toothed leaves, a few small pink flowers near the top and fine pale roots, on plain cream paper.
prompt: This is already a watercolour. Match its washes: one pale green per leaf.
tip: Pull the roots with the very tip of a small brush, in one movement each.
curationNote: One focus subject on plain paper, already a watercolour. A lovely study to copy stroke for stroke.

title: William the Hippo
subject: creatures
alt: The Met's blue faience hippopotamus, nicknamed William, standing on four short legs, painted with dark outlines of lotus flowers and leaves, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint the whole hippo in one blue wash, then draw the lotus plants on it once it is dry.
tip: Keep the blue a touch paler on the back, where the light lands.
curationNote: One clear subject on a plain grey ground, sharp, with one strong colour. The Met's best-loved object.

title: Yellow Bowl
subject: objects
alt: A plain porcelain bowl in a smooth, bright yellow glaze with a pale foot ring, seen from the side against a plain grey background.
prompt: One yellow curve. Paint the bowl in one wash and add the inside shadow once it dries.
tip: Grey the yellow for the shadow with a touch of violet rather than black.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp. A quick warm-up.

title: Coral-Red Bottle Vase
subject: objects
alt: A glossy coral-red porcelain bottle vase with a round body and a long thin neck, with bright highlights on its shoulder, against a plain grey background.
prompt: One red shape. Save the highlights as paper before the colour goes on.
tip: Deepen the red toward the bottom and the far side while it is still wet.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp, in one bold colour.

candidate.medium: Stoneware with white slip and glaze

title: Cream Stoneware Dish
subject: objects
alt: A shallow cream-glazed stoneware dish with gently flared sides on a small foot, seen from the side against a plain grey background.
prompt: Paint the grey background round the dish and leave the dish almost as paper.
tip: One pale warm grey for the inside curve is all the shading it needs.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground. White on grey, a quick warm-up.

title: Peach-Bloom Box
subject: objects
alt: A small round lidded porcelain box in a glossy peach-bloom glaze, pink across the top fading to mottled green at the edge, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Wet the whole box and let the pink run into the green.
tip: Leave the two bright highlights as bare paper from the start.
curationNote: One small, simple shape on a plain grey ground. Soft colour changes to practise.

title: Lapis Fish
subject: creatures
alt: A small fish amulet carved in violet-blue lapis lazuli with pale flecks and a forked tail, lying on its side on a plain white background.
prompt: One blue fish. Wet it, drop in violet, and dab out a few pale flecks.
tip: Lift the pale flecks with a damp brush while the blue is still wet.
curationNote: One small, simple shape on a plain ground. A quick warm-up.

candidate.creator: Hakusanjin Hokui
candidate.medium: Woodblock print; ink and color on paper

title: Copper Pheasant
subject: creatures
alt: A Japanese woodblock print of a copper pheasant walking with its head lowered, a long barred tail sweeping behind it, a red face patch and dark body feathers, on plain cream paper with a brushed signature.
prompt: Paint the long tail in one confident sweep, then build the dark body on top.
tip: Keep the tail's bars loose: a few broken strokes along its length are enough.
curationNote: One clear subject on plain paper. Already a print in soft colours, so it translates well.

title: Red Jasper Hippo
subject: creatures
alt: A small hippopotamus carved from polished red jasper, lying down with its head raised, against a plain white to grey background.
prompt: One red shape. Wet it, drop in a darker red underneath, and stop.
tip: Leave a sliver of paper along the back for the polish.
curationNote: One small, simple shape on a plain ground, sharp. A quick warm-up in one colour.

title: Silver Jar
subject: objects
alt: A small Egyptian silver jar with a round body, a tall straight neck and a gold rim, softly mottled and dull, against a plain grey background.
prompt: Silver is mostly reflected grey. Paint the dark streaks and leave the highlights as paper.
tip: Keep the gold rim for last, as one thin warm line.
curationNote: One simple object on a plain grey ground, sharp. Good practice for metal.

title: Falcon with Spread Wings
subject: creatures
alt: An Egyptian faience inlay of a falcon with its wings spread wide and its head turned, holding a ring in its claws, in faded blue-green, red and cream, on a plain pale background.
prompt: Paint the wing shapes as two big washes first; the feathers can be suggested on top.
tip: A few dry-brush strokes across each wing will read as feathers without painting every one.
curationNote: One clear subject on a plain pale ground, sharp, with a bold, graphic shape.

title: Roses in a Dark Vase
subject: still-life
alt: A gouache study of pink roses and grey-green leaves spilling from a dark red and black urn-shaped vase, on toned brown paper with faint pencil lines left unpainted.
prompt: Paint the roses first while the paper is fresh, then the dark vase last.
tip: Keep the vase's black warm by mixing it from burnt umber and ultramarine.
curationNote: A simple arrangement on a plain toned ground. A study rather than a finished painting, which suits practice.

title: Carnelian Falcon
subject: creatures
alt: A tiny falcon amulet carved in translucent orange carnelian, with a drilled hole for hanging, on a plain white background.
prompt: One orange shape. Let the colour pool darker at the base.
tip: Leave the lightest part of the stone as bare paper so it glows.
curationNote: One tiny, simple shape on a plain white ground. A quick warm-up in one glowing colour.

title: Resting Pigeon
subject: creatures
alt: A painting of a single plump pigeon resting, its white feathers edged in pale grey, rust-red patches across its back, an iridescent grey-green neck and pink feet, on plain pale tan paper.
prompt: Leave the white feathers as paper and paint only their grey edges and the red patches.
tip: Glaze the neck with a thin wash of terre verte over dry grey for the sheen.
curationNote: One clear subject on plain paper. White feathers are good practice for leaving the paper.
